title: Table Four, Table Six
subject: On a blind date set up by his sister, Colin sits at table four and Jan at table six of a Liverpool tea room, each secretly brought a best friend to spy from the next table, and it is the two spies who start talking.
caption: Merseybeat, early-1960s British beat group sound. Chiming twelve-string Rickenbacker jangle on open chords, driving melodic bass guitar, crisp snare-and-tom backbeat with ride cymbal, handclaps on the choruses, bright electric rhythm guitar. Dry 1963 tape sound with slight saturation, punchy mono-leaning mix. Male lead tenor with a second male voice in close two-part harmony, cheeky and bright delivery. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 132 BPM, A major. Cheeky, bright, jangly. No rap, no autotune, no synthesizers, no electronic drums, no distorted modern guitars, no vocal effects.
lyrics:
[Intro - twelve-string jangle, bass, snare count-in]

[Verse 1]
Our Sue said wear the blue cravat
Sit at table four, don't fuss
She's at table six, you'll see
Reading menus upside down

[Pre-Chorus]
I brought my mate, she brought hers too
Each behind a pot of tea

[Chorus]
Oh, the spies are talking, spies are talking
While the two of us just stare
Oh, the spies are talking, spies are talking
Over scones at table five

[Verse 2]
Dave is passing her friend the jam
Pat is laughing at his jokes
We're both pretending not to look
Two cold cups and nothing said

[Pre-Chorus]
He brought a mate, she brought one too
Now the mates are leaving us

[Chorus]
Oh, the spies are laughing, spies are laughing
And we sit here with the bill
Oh, the spies are walking, spies are walking
Out the door, arm in arm

[Bridge - drums and clap only]
Shall we push the tables together

[Chorus]
Oh, the spies are married, spies are married
By the summer, so they say
Oh, we're still talking, still talking
Over scones at table five

[Outro - jangle and bass, ring-out ending]
Table four, table six
